title: Canonical generators and normalization of pulled principal Koszul towers
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, with independent scheme and coefficient universes. For a scheme morphism $g:X\to Y$ use the completed module categories $\mathcal M_W$, the ordinary module pullback $G_g$ with its specified adjunction unit $\eta$, and the actual small pro-etale base-change functor $g_{\mathrm{Proet}}$ of [def-a1-integral-completed-tower-pullback-universes]. Define $G$ on unbounded cochain complexes by applying $G_g$ to every term and differential; define $\operatorname{diagramPull}$ on strict towers by postcomposition with $G$. For $M\in\mathcal M_Y$, $V\in Y_{\mathrm{Proet}}$, and $x\in M(V)$, define $\operatorname{generator}_g(x)=\eta_M(V)(x)\in(G_gM)(g_{\mathrm{Proet}}V)$. Use the actual sheafified total-tensor summand generator $\tau_{p,q}$ of [def-coef-ringed-tensor-hom-model]. For the principal mapping-cone Koszul complexes $Q_{W,n}=[R_W\xrightarrow{t^{n+1}}R_W]$ of [def-a1-principal-completed-koszul-towers], define $e_{W,n,0}:R_W\to Q_{W,n}^0$ by the target cone inclusion and $e_{W,n,-1}:R_W\to Q_{W,n}^{-1}$ by the shifted source cone inclusion, both preceded by the inverse of the standard degree-zero single-complex identification. Index these bases by $\mathrm{negative}\in\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$, with degrees $d(\mathrm{false})=0$ and $d(\mathrm{true})=-1$. Put $H_W(P)_n=P\otimes Q_{W,n}$, with the specified strict transitions, by the existing source tower of [def-a1-principal-completed-koszul-towers]. For an isomorphism of strict towers $e:\operatorname{diagramPull}(H_Y(P))\cong H_X(GP)$ define $\operatorname{KoszulNormalization}(P,e)$ to mean that for every $n\in\mathbf N$, either basis degree $i\in\{-1,0\}$, $p,k\in\mathbf Z$ with $p+i=k$, $V\in Y_{\mathrm{Proet}}$, $x\in P^p(V)$ and $b\in R_X(g_{\mathrm{Proet}}V)$, one has
$$e_{n}^{k}\bigl(b\,\operatorname{generator}_g(\tau_{p,i}(x,e_{Y,n,i}(1)))\bigr)=\tau_{p,i}\bigl(b\,\operatorname{generator}_g(x),e_{X,n,i}(1)\bigr).$$
No goodness, boundedness, coefficient-map flatness or invertibility-of-$\ell$ hypothesis is imposed.
